title: Isomorphic Shift Domain Definitions
description: Canonical definitions of all domains involved in isomorphic shifts

canonical_representation.description: Type signature in canonical form (e.g., 'instruction(verb: atom, args: list)')

constraints.description: Structural constraints that all members must satisfy

description.const: User-facing instructions: EmojiCode, HolyC, Python, JavaScript, Ada surface syntax

canonical_representation.const: surface_instruction(source_lang: atom, verb: atom, args: map)

constraints: source_lang in {emoji, holyc, python, javascript, ada}
args is valid map for the language
no shell metacharacters in any string argument
syntax must parse in source language
invariants: verb_identity — verb remains unchanged through round-trip

description.const: Normalized intermediate form: deterministic CBOR-encoded instruction

canonical_representation.const: canonical_instruction(verb: atom, args: list, required_perms: list, hash: blake3)

constraints: verb is normalized atom (lowercase, no whitespace)
args is ordered list (not map) in canonical order
hash is deterministic Blake3 of CBOR encoding
CBOR encoding must be canonical (RFC 7049 Section 3.9)
invariants: determinism — same input always produces same hash

description.const: Prolog/Datalog term representation for logical reasoning

canonical_representation.const: logic_term(functor: atom, args: list) or logic_term(atomic_value)

constraints: functor is valid atom (letters, digits, underscore)
no free variables in canonical form (all instantiated or explicitly universally quantified)
term must be ground (no unbound logic variables)
invariants: functor_identity — same functor as instruction verb
argument_identity — same argument count and structure
type_correspondence — types correspond to Prolog types

description.const: Logic reasoning result with authorization proof from Prolog

canonical_representation.const: authorized_decision(agent: atom, decision: logic_term, proof_id: hash, timestamp: u64)

constraints: agent is known agent class (sentinel, oracle, builder, archivist, berserker)
proof_id is Blake3 hash of Prolog query trace
agent must have required trust level

description.const: Executable runtime command: HolyC, Rust, Erlang, LLVM bytecode

canonical_representation.const: runtime_command(target: atom, opcode: atom, operands: list, required_context: map)

constraints: target in {holyc, rust, erlang, llvm, ada}
opcode is valid instruction mnemonic for target
invariants: semantics_preservation — runtime behavior matches decision semantics
target_executability — command is valid on target
safety_preservation — no unsafe operations not approved by decision

description.const: Formal proof goal in Lean 4 or Agda

canonical_representation.const: proof_obligation(theorem_name: atom, hypotheses: list, goal: formula, required_by: atom)

constraints: goal is well-formed formula in proof system
required_by identifies which shift/component needs this proof
formula syntax must be valid Lean 4 or Agda

description.const: Invocation of formal verifier (Lean 4, Agda) with result

canonical_representation.const: verifier_invocation(proof_id: hash, verifier: atom, status: atom, proof_code: string, timestamp: u64)

constraints: proof_id is Blake3 hash of obligation
proof_code is valid Lean 4 or Agda code
invariants: status_integrity — status reflects actual verification result

description.const: Runtime event from agent or system: state transition, policy application, output

canonical_representation.const: execution_event(event_id: hash, timestamp: u64, agent: atom, action: atom, payload: map, parent_receipt_hash: option(hash))

constraints: event_id is Blake3 hash (deterministic from content)

description.const: Prolog/Datalog fact representing a runtime event

canonical_representation.const: logic_event_fact(event_id: hash, agent: atom, action: atom, outcome: atom, worm_seal: hash)

constraints: event_id is Blake3 hash of execution event
invariants: event_correspondence — fact describes the same event

description.const: Immutable WORM-sealed proof of execution and authorization

canonical_representation.const: receipt_record(receipt_id: hash, event_id: hash, authorization_proof: hash, verification_status: atom, worm_seal: hash, timestamp: u64)

constraints: authorization_proof is hash of Prolog query result
invariants: event_ancestry — receipt_id traces to original event

description.const: Jupyter/IPython notebook cell with metadata and sealed outputs

canonical_representation.const: notebook_cell(cell_id: hash, cell_type: atom, source: string, outputs: list, execution_count: int, metadata: map)

constraints: cell_id is Blake3 hash of (source, execution_count)
outputs list contains cell outputs (empty if not executed)
invariants: output_sealing — outputs sealed once execution complete

description.const: Prolog/Datalog fact encoding notebook cell semantics

canonical_representation.const: logic_cell_fact(cell_id: hash, cell_type: atom, instructions_extracted: list, proof_obligations: list, worm_seal: hash)

constraints: proof_obligations is list of proof_obligation terms

description.const: Values specific to runtime environment: integers, floats, strings, arrays, capabilities

canonical_representation.const: runtime_value(type: atom, value: any, runtime_context: map)

constraints: type in {i32, i64, u32, u64, f32, f64, f128, bool, string, bytes, array, map, capability}
f32/f64/f128 must be finite (±inf, NaN explicitly marked)
runtime_context specifies source runtime (rust, holyc, erlang, etc.)

canonical_representation.const: canonical_value(type: atom, value: cbor_bytes, type_tag: atom)

constraints: type in {integer, rational, float, boolean, atom, string, bytes, list, map, tagged_union, capability_ref, hash_ref}
type_tag provides type information for deserializer
floats marked as such (not ambiguous with integers)
arrays have explicit shape/rank in type_tag
invariants: type_preservation — runtime type maps to canonical type
determinism — same input always produces same CBOR
no_precision_loss — exact representation in rational/big-int if needed
